text:
A: Hello? Oh dear, have I got it? Sorry, it said "waiting for the host" and then it just sort of dropped me in.
B: Yeah, you're on.
A: Lovely. I'm Graham. Newark, Nottinghamshire.
B: Callum. Basingstoke.
A: Basingstoke. That's, er, off the M3, isn't it? I went to a conference there once, years ago. Can't remember a thing about it except the roundabouts.
B: Yeah, that's all there is, to be fair.
A: Ha. Well, we've got the A46, which is our cross to bear. Are you at school, Callum, or working?
B: Both. A-levels, and I work Saturdays in a sports shop.
A: Good lad. What are you doing for your A-levels?
B: Business, Economics, PE.
A: Economics. I'd have been hopeless at that. I can just about do the firm's accounts, and that's only because Janet sits next to me with a pencil.
B: What firm?
A: Oh, sorry, I'm a solicitor. Small high-street practice, wills and probate, a bit of conveyancing. Been doing it since, er, nineteen seventy-something. Before you were thought of, put it that way.
B: Is it good money though? Like, being a solicitor.
A: Er, well. It depends where you are. The big London firms, the young ones are on silly money, but they work all hours. In a little place like ours it's comfortable, but you don't get rich doing wills in Newark. I get paid in cups of tea and people telling me about their grandad.
B: Right. I'm not doing uni anyway. I want a degree apprenticeship, like finance, at a bank. Then you're getting paid and you've not got the debt. Then eventually I'll do my own thing, reselling, clothing maybe. Make more than my dad by twenty-five.
A: Well, that's a plan. More than I had at your age, I'll tell you that. I just sort of did what my teacher said.
B: Yeah, most people do.
A: Is that an Arsenal shirt behind you?
B: Yeah. My dad's team, so I didn't really get a choice.
A: No, you never do. Mine's Forest. Born into it, sort of thing. I'd show you my mug, but it's full of pens.
B: Forest are alright this season, to be fair. Better than people thought.
A: Don't say that, you'll jinx them. My son-in-law takes me now and again, and every time I go they lose, so I've been told to stay at home.
B: Ha. That's like my five-a-side lot. Every week there's an argument about whether something's a foul. Every single week.
A: Oh, I played cricket for a village side, and it was the same with lbw. Forty years on, there's a chap in our pub who still says I wasn't out in nineteen eighty-two. And I'll be honest, I probably was out. Er, where was I. Oh yes, do you drive yet?
B: Learning. I failed my first test though. Examiner was a joke, honestly.
A: Ah, I failed my first one as well. Went round a roundabout the wrong way in Grantham. In fairness to the examiner, that one was probably my fault.
B: Mine wasn't. It was a minor that he made a serious.
A: Well, you'll get it next time. My grandson's the same, he's
B: How old is he?
